semantic_changes: No production logic is replaced or patched; the harness uses the crate's public API only. The helpers added for the new cases read decided entries through read_decided_suffix/read.

scope.description: One test target with three deterministic in-process cases over real OmniPaxos instances driven by explicit tick and route steps: (a) batched_mixed_proposals - three nodes, batch_size 4, eight entries proposed on the leader and eight on a follower, compared for identical decided vectors, complete proposed-value coverage and index/content consistency; (b) leader_change_prefix - three nodes, batch_size 2, a decided prefix, removal of the leader, election of a replacement, further entries, then recovery of the old leader from its persisted storage, compared for prefix preservation and identical vectors; (c) stale_decided_vs_compacted_follower - the previously established recovery/compaction case, unchanged.
assumptions: Node pids {1,2,3}, configuration_id 1, majority quorum, deterministic message routing; no threads, no timers, no network.

Crash is modelled by removing the instance while keeping its storage handle, and recovery by rebuilding from that handle; the durable state is therefore the state the node had written before the crash.
Decision comparison reads the decided suffix through the public API while nothing is compacted in the two new cases, so element positions correspond to log indices.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled, matching the controller's cargo test invocation.
excluded: Snapshot-capable entry types and the persistent backend are not exercised by these two cases (they are covered by the contrast experiment).
Larger clusters, other quorum shapes, concurrent multi-leader proposals and message reordering beyond the deterministic schedule are not exercised.

basis.prefix: Cluster::new(nodes, batch_size) builds OmniPaxos instances (pids 1,2,3) over shared in-memory storage handles and pump_until ticks and routes until a (Leader, Accept) exists. Case (a): with batch_size 4 the harness appends TestEntry(0..8) on the elected leader and TestEntry(100..108) on one follower, then pump_until every node reports decided_idx 16; it then collects each node's decided vector via read_decided_suffix(0), compares the three vectors, compares the sorted values with the proposed multiset, and for every node and index checks that read(idx) returns the vector element at that index, emitting case_result_batched. Case (b): with batch_size 2 it appends TestEntry(0..6) on the leader, waits until all nodes report decided_idx 6, emits leader_change_admitted with the prefix, removes the leader instance, pump_until a new (Leader, Accept) exists, appends TestEntry(200..204) on the new leader, waits until all surviving nodes report decided_idx 10, and emits case_result_leader_change with the new leader's identity, prefix preservation and vector equality; it then rebuilds the old leader from its storage handle and pump_until every node reports decided_idx 10 with equal vectors, emitting case_result_leader_change_recovered. Case (c) is unchanged from the earlier revision and emits setup, case_admitted, trim_applied, new_leader_established, log_sync_outcome and run_summary.
basis.responsibility: For case (a) the responsibility under test is the leader's batched accept path and each follower's batched append together with the reported accepted index; for case (b) it is the synchronisation and adoption path used after a leader change and on recovery; case (c) keeps the previously asserted responsibility for the below-compaction log-update request.

comparisons.description: Stale-decided case (unchanged): the healthy follower handles the stale node's Prepare without aborting.
With batch_size 4 and concurrent leader/follower proposals, every node reports the same decided vector.
Each node's entry readable at index i equals the element that node reports for index i.
After removing the leader and electing a replacement, the decided prefix is unchanged on every surviving node.
The old leader, rebuilt from its persisted storage, converges to the same decided vector as the survivors.

knowledge.assertion: the non-snapshot branch reads get_suffix(common_prefix_idx) with no comparison against the responder's compacted index

before.description: Three scenarios in one test, each driving one responder replica through a legal leader prefix (Prepare, AcceptSync with six entries and decided_idx 6, forwarded Compaction::Trim(6)) and then a legal Prepare with decided_idx 3 and an older accepted round: (a) snapshots disabled with the in-memory backend, (b) snapshots enabled with the in-memory backend, (c) snapshots disabled with the persistent RocksDB backend. The outcome of handling that Prepare is reported per case.
assumptions: The messages delivered are the shapes a real leader produces (Prepare, AcceptSync/log_sync, forwarded Compaction::Trim, and a later Prepare from a node whose decided index lags); the responder is a real OmniPaxos instance whose state is produced by those messages rather than set directly.

The three-node configuration is used only for construction; the responder is node 2 and the sender is node 1. No tick, no election and no message routing are involved, so nothing depends on scheduling.

AcceptSync carries sync_idx 0 with a six-entry suffix and decided_idx 6, i.e. the update a leader sends to a peer that has no entries yet; the forwarded Trim(6) is legal because the responder's decided index is already 6.

The state this harness reaches (accepted_idx 6, decided_idx 6, compacted_idx 6, accepted round newer than the preparing node's) is the same state the earlier multi-node experiment reached through real message exchange.
Dev profile with overflow checks enabled, matching the controller's cargo test invocation.

For case (c) the responder uses PersistentStorage opened on a fresh temporary directory, with the same entry type as case (a); the temporary directory is kept alive for the case and dropped afterwards.
Cases (a) and (b) use the in-memory backend behind a shared handle so the same code path is exercised with and without snapshots.
excluded: Release-profile behaviour, the persistent storage backend, and cluster-level consequences after the abort are not measured here.
Only the snapshot/non-snapshot distinction is varied; cluster size, batch size, trim index and quorum are held equal.
Behaviour when overflow checks are disabled (release profile) is not measured for any case.

prefix.before: scenario(case, snapshots, outcome_event, store, mk) builds one OmniPaxos instance (pid 2, nodes 1,2,3) over the supplied storage and then calls, in order: handle_incoming(Prepare{n: (1,1,pid 1), decided_idx: 0, n_accepted: 0, accepted_idx: 0}); handle_incoming(AcceptSync{n: (1,1,pid 1), seq_num: (session 0, counter 1), decided_idx: 6, log_sync: {decided_snapshot: None, suffix: six entries 0..5, sync_idx: 0, stopsign: None}}); handle_incoming(Compaction::Trim(6)). It then emits case_started and state_reached (both carrying case and use_snapshots, plus accepted_idx/decided_idx/compacted_idx on state_reached), and finally calls handle_incoming(Prepare{n: (1,2,pid 1), decided_idx: 3, n_accepted: 0, accepted_idx: 6}) inside catch_unwind, emitting the case-specific outcome event with case, use_snapshots, outcome, panic message and the three indices. The test runs the prefix three times: 'nosnapshot_entry' (UseSnapshots false, in-memory backend, event log_sync_outcome_nosnapshot), 'snapshot_entry' (UseSnapshots true, in-memory backend, event log_sync_outcome_snapshot) and 'persistent_backend_entry' (UseSnapshots false, PersistentStorage opened on a fresh tempdir, event log_sync_outcome_persistent).

responsibility.before: The three cases separate which captured component decides the outcome: the core's log-update construction selects its branch from T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() and the deciding node's decided index; with the in-memory backend the abort is raised by its unchecked subtraction inside MemoryStorage::get_suffix, and with the persistent backend the storage returns an error for the same request and the core's own expect in create_log_sync raises the abort.

revision_reason: Follow-up basis: this revision returns to the cluster harness and adds two decision-formation cases (batched mixed proposals; leader change plus recovery of the old leader) to the recovery case it already carries, so the contract between the reported accepted index and the entries a node holds, and the adoption path after a leader change, are both measured in the same target. The preceding contrast revision remains the fixed artifact for the branch-selection and backend questions.
